thread:
maria: quick follow-up on fused attention variants — thinking about exposing a runtime hint so the serving layer can prefer a dropout-free path and select rope handling without touching model artifacts. want to discuss compatibility and rollout.
kai: +1. main concern is KV cache layout. switching rope or qkv layout at runtime can change past-kv offsets.
devon: can you sketch the minimal API you have in mind? per-model metadata or per-request hint?
maria: proposal: runtime_hints live in model metadata and can be overridden per-request. example payload:

```json
{"runtime_hints": {"attention_mode": "fused_qkv", "dropout_free": true, "rope_variant": "rotary_v2"}}
```

Runtime chooses the most optimal kernel that matches model + hint; if none match, fallback to safe path.
olga: per-request override is useful for A/B evals, but rollout complexity spikes. need canary keys so we can target small traffic.
kai: we must also record kernel_id + rope_variant in telemetry for each request. otherwise ops cant trace perf regressions to kernel choices.
devon: another compatibility issue: many exported models keep q/k/v as separate tensors. fused-qkv kernels expect interleaved qkv memory. we need either a cheap conversion or separate kernels.
maria: agree. runtime should provide a lightweight conversion step at model load if memory allows, otherwise do the conversion lazily on first invocation and cache the converted buffer. pseudocode:

```py
if model.weights.qkv_layout == 'separate' and runtime_prefers('fused_qkv'):
  schedule(async_convert_qkv(model))
```

olga: conversion must be async so cold-start requests aren't blocked. also we should emit a memory-spike metric when conversion happens.
kai: about dropout-free: inference should drop dropout ops. but if a customer runs evals that expect dropout behavior (stochastic evals), we need an explicit opt-in flag so we don't alter semantics silently.
maria: plan: default is safe (no automatic switch). add feature-flag `enable_dropout_free_autoswitch` for canaries. model authors can also set `dropout_free: true` in metadata when they certify the model.
devon: suggestion: exporter-level tag `fused_capable=true`. if model claims fused_capable then runtime can be more aggressive. avoids unexpected transforms for third-party models.
olga: ops / rollout checklist: per-model rollout metadata, metric guardrails (latency p95, error rate), automatic rollback if anomalies detected.
infra-bot: TASK CREATED: TASK-1427 schedule async qkv-convert job for model loads. TASK-1428 add kernel_id and rope_variant to request telemetry schema.
maria: thanks — i'll update the RFC follow-up doc with explicit API examples + rollout checklist and link. cc @kai @devon for telemetry schema review. :thumbsup:
